- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model underreacts to downward drift; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of prior 18-day history.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% in first 5 days, reduce subsequent forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence with observed trend.
